Two constants of the estimates are bounded by finite computations, and with these bounds the $3$-adic valuation exceeds the size and the denominators together by more than $4.5$ bits per $n^2$. An appendix gives a second proof, independent of the first, which adapts to $\zeta_3(5)$ and the modular curve $X_0(3)$ a determinant argument that a preprint of Yi gives for $\zeta_7(3)$, and which rests on published theorems on overconvergent modular forms.

papers.title: Optimal affinity of autocatalytic networks beyond gross stoichiometry
papers.abstract: An explicit reversible autocatalytic network has a unique global maximum of controlled production whose affinity exponential is strictly below its gross stoichiometric seed ratio. This refutes the proposed general lower bound. We identify a response-profile capacity that retains the missing kinetic information, analyze a literal recycling family approaching the source boundary and give a zero-diagonal counterexample. Under the stated rooted accessibility and response hypotheses, a local mass-action realization theorem makes the capacity sharp; an explicit power family supplies global maxima, while interacting cores delimit broader claims. The registered Lean project verifies the original refutation and checks the explicit witness against the literature conventions. Broader historical formal evidence and conventional arguments are distinguished in the manuscript and supporting claim map.

papers.title: Oscillator representations of quantum affine orthosymplectic superalgebras II
papers.abstract: As a continuation of our study on quantum affine spin-oscillator correspondence, we introduce a category of $q$-oscillator representations of quantum affine superalgebras of type $XB$ ($X=B,D$) and construct irreducible objects in a uniform way. Under the truncation functor inspired by the theory of super duality, they are related to finite-dimensional irreducible representations of $U_q(D^{(2)}_{n+1})$ ($X=B$) or $U_q(B^{(1)}_{n})$ ($X=D$). We also considerably streamline our previous arguments, which clarifies how our construction can be understood as a quantum affinization of classical super duality.

papers.title: Persistent (Co)Homology in Matrix Multiplication Time
papers.abstract: Most algorithms for computing persistent homology do so by tracking cycles that represent homology classes. There are many choices of such cycles, and specific choices have found different uses in applications. Although it is known that persistence diagrams can be computed in matrix multiplication time [8] for the more general case of zigzag persistent homology, it is not clear how to extract cycle representatives, especially if specific representatives are desired. In this paper, we provide the same matrix multiplication bound for computing representatives for the two choices common in applications in the case of ordinary persistent (co)homology. We first provide a fast version of the reduction algorithm, which is simpler than the algorithm in [8], but returns a different set of representatives than the standard algorithm [6] We then give a fast version of a different variant called the row algorithm [4], which returns the same representatives as the standard algorithm.

papers.title: Point Counts of Cluster Varieties of Marked Surfaces Over Finite Fields
papers.abstract: We establish formulae for point counts of cluster varieties of cluster algebras of marked surfaces, possibly with punctures. We then establish formulae for the number of non-deep points in these cluster varieties over $\mathbb{F}_2$, which gives us the number of algebraic tori necessary to cover the cluster manifold over $\mathbb{F}_2$. We also show that these formulae satisfy certain recurrence relations.

papers.title: Properties of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Manifolds
papers.abstract: We continue the study of compact holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds $X$ that we introduced recently by expanding the discussion to include non-K\"ahler hyperbolicity issues and a differential calculus based on what we call the Lie derivative with respect to a $(0,\,q)$-form with values in the holomorphic tangent bundle of $X$. We also propose the notion of $p$-contact deformations for which we prove a Bogomolov-Tian-Todorov-type unobstructedness theorem to order two. This kind of small deformations of the complex structure is related to the essential horizontal deformations that we introduced in our previous work and forms part of a wider on-going project aimed at developing a non-K\"ahler mirror symmetry theory that was first tested on the Iwasawa manifold and subsequently on Calabi-Yau page-$1$-$\partial\bar\partial$-manifolds.

papers.title: Quadratic hulls of osculating varieties of rational normal curves
papers.abstract:
Let $T^p c_r$ be the $p$-osculating variety of the rational normal curve $c_r\subset\mathbb{P}S^r(\mathbb{C}^2)$. We study its quadratic hull, the scheme defined by the quadratic equations vanishing on $T^p c_r$. For $r\ge2p+3$, we prove that this scheme is a complete intersection of $\binom{r-2p}{2}$ quadrics whenever \[
  p\ge\binom{r-2p-1}{2}. \] When the inequality is strict, the hull is integral and strictly contains $T^p c_r$. On the boundary its support is reducible, except for $(p,r)=(1,5)$, where the hull equals the osculating variety. The proof is local at the highest weight point. Koornwinder's relation between Clebsch--Gordan coefficients and Hahn polynomials leads to a description of the tangent-cone equations in which each antidiagonal becomes an ordinary polynomial space of bounded degree. An incidence estimate then gives a normal integral tangent cone in the strict range, and the $SL_2$-action turns this local statement into global integrality.

papers.title: Quantization in polarization via transverse Poincar\'e-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
papers.abstract:
We construct, for every prequantizable symplectic manifold $(M,\omega,L)$ equipped with a nonsingular polarization, a deformation quantization $(C_M^\infty[[\hbar]],\star)$ together with a filtered sheaf of subalgebras $C_{M,\hbar}^{(<\infty)}$ that admits an exact action on polarized sections of $L^{\otimes k}$ for each $k\in\mathbb Z^+$. This extends the Kostant--Souriau action of polarization-preserving functions.
  The main geometric ingredient is a transverse PBW theory associated with a Nirenberg integrable distribution $P$. For any locally free $P$-modules $E$ and $E'$, we construct a PBW isomorphism for the bundle of transverse differential operators from $E$ to $E'$. This extends the PBW theorem for Lie pairs of Laurent-Gengoux--Sti\'enon--Xu to the setting of $P$-modules.
  After specializing $\hbar= \tfrac{\sqrt{-1}}{k}$, we obtain a sheaf $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ of level-$k$ quantizable functions and prove that its action identifies $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ with the sheaf of transverse differential operators on $L^{\otimes k}$. In the K\"ahler case, this recovers the construction of Chan--Leung--Li.
  Finally, for standard symplectic tori with real polarizations, we compare our construction with Toeplitz-type operators and obtain their semiclassical asymptotic expansions.

papers.title: Quaternionic Heisenberg-Robertson-Schrodinger and Maccone-Pati Uncertainty Principles
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a quaternionic Hilbert space. Let $A: \mathcal{D}(A)\subseteq \mathcal{Q}\to \mathcal{Q}$ and $B:\mathcal{D}(B)\subseteq \mathcal{Q}\to \mathcal{Q}$ be possibly unbounded self-adjoint linear operators. Then for all $h \in \mathcal{D}(AB)\cap \mathcal{D}(BA)$ with $\|h\|=1$, we show that \begin{align*} (1) \quad \quad \quad \Delta _h(A)\Delta _h(B)\geq \frac{\sqrt{|\langle \{A,B\}h, h \rangle -2\langle Ah, h \rangle\langle Bh, h \rangle|^2+|\langle [A,B]h, h \rangle |^2}}{2} \end{align*} and \begin{align*} (2) \quad \quad \quad \Delta _h(A)^2+ \Delta _h(B)^2 \geq \frac{|\langle (A+B)h, y \rangle|^2+|\langle (A-B)h, y \rangle|^2}{2}, \quad \forall y \in \mathcal{Q} \text{ satisfying } \|y\|\leq1 \text{ and } \langle h, y \rangle =0, \end{align*} where $ \Delta _h(A)\coloneqq \|Ah-\langle Ah, h \rangle h \|$. We call Inequality (1) as quaternionic Heisenberg-Robertson-Schrodinger uncertainty principle and Inequality (2) as quaternionic Maccone-Pati uncertainty principle.

papers.title: Real Nullstellensatz for nilpotent Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We prove a real Nullstellensatz for the universal enveloping algebra U(g) of a nilpotent finite-dimensional real Lie algebra g: An ideal of U(g) is real if and only if it is the intersection of kernels of irreducible integrable *-representations of U(g) by (in general unbounded) operators on a Hilbert space. For this, we build upon some classical results about the complexification of U(g) that lead to a complex Nullstellensatz (every semiprime ideal is the intersection of primitive ideals), but focus only on the ``real points'', i.e., the *-representations on Hilbert spaces. On the technical side, this requires to take into account an involution of U(g), namely, the antipode of its Hopf algebra structure, which goes into the definition of real ideals of U(g). Our result is the first noncommutative real Nullstellensatz for *-algebras with unbounded irreducible *-representations, demonstrating how methods of real algebraic geometry can lead to results about operator *-algebras also in situations where C*-algebraic methods fail.

papers.title: Relative $P$-Ideals of Hypergraphs and Ultrafilter Spectra
papers.abstract: We study ideals of hypergraphs of finite uniformity under countable upper bounds modulo finite vertex covers. The canonical ideal generated by a free filter and finite weak colorings has this relative $P$-property exactly when the filter is the intersection of finitely many $P$-points. The classification is preserved by adjoining hypergraphs that are locally finite after a finite vertex deletion. The corresponding extension of a trace ideal induces capture ideals on increasing sequences. These are $\sigma$-ideals exactly for $P$-filters, and their uniformities are $\max\{\pi\chi(\mathcal{F}),\mathfrak{d}\}$. For an ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$, the arity-two capture ideal equals the Louveau ideal exactly when $\mathcal{U}$ is a $P$-point. Successive capture ideals decrease with the arity, and equality characterizes $Q$-points. Every strict inclusion is witnessed by a closed set. Thus a non-$Q$ $P$-point yields a decreasing sequence of $\sigma$-ideals, distinguished by closed sets, with equal uniformities. We also establish invariance under locally finite witness enlargements and analyze Stone kernels and countable block products. Consistently, nested ray-positive $P$-sets have the same singleton endpoint spectrum and different ray transversal numbers.

papers.title: Relative mirror symmetry, theta functions and the Gamma conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Fano variety, and $D\subset X$ be an snc anticanonical divisor. We study relative mirror symmetry for the log Calabi--Yau pair $(X,D)$. (1) We prove a relative mirror theorem for snc pairs without assuming the divisors are nef. (2) We study theta functions associated with the pair $(X,D)$. (3) We introduce functions on the mirror that are obtained from the higher-degree part of the big relative quantum cohomology. As an application, we use these new ingredients in relative mirror symmetry to prove a version of the mirror symmetric Gamma conjecture for $X$ for $\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{pt}}$ in this setting, where the Landau--Ginzburg potential is defined as a sum of theta functions.

papers.title: Representing Vineyard Modules
papers.abstract: Time-series of persistence diagrams, more commonly known as vineyards, are a useful way to capture how multi-scale topological features vary over time. However, we do lose significant information in how the persistent homology at different time stamps relate to each other. A natural algebraic version of vineyards is a time series of persistence modules equipped with interleaving maps between the persistence modules at different time stamps. We call this a vineyard module. In this paper we will set up the framework for representing a vineyard module via an indexed set of vines alongside a collection of matrices. We outline an algorithmic way to transform the bases of the persistence modules at each time step within the vineyard module to make the matrices within this representation as simple as possible. With some reasonable assumptions on the vineyard modules, this simplified representation can be completely described (up to isomorphism) by the associated vineyard and a vector of finite length. While this vineyard and vector representation is not necessarily unique we can prove that the vector will always be the zero vector when the vineyard module is isomorphic to the direct sum of vine modules. We also show uniqueness when the vineyard module contains two vines (over field $\mathbb{F}_2$) and can characterise and count which are realisable, giving a complete account of isomorphism classes of vineyard modules with two vines. To define and analyse this approach we first must set up a lot of preliminary results about changes of bases for pairs of persistence modules where we are given $\varepsilon$-interleaving maps for sufficiently close $\varepsilon$. This new perspective on vineyards also provides a new approach to the study of multi-parameter persistence modules.

papers.title: Revisiting Gamma conjecture I: counterexamples and modifications
papers.abstract: We continue investigation of asymptotics of quantum differential equation for Fano manifolds, with a special regard to Gamma conjecture I and its underlying Conjecture $\mathcal{O}$. We introduce the A-model conifold value, a symplectic invariant of a Fano manifold, and propose modifications for Gamma conjecture I based on this new definition. We discuss an interplay of birational transformations with an extension of Gamma conjecture I over the K\"ahler moduli space. These heuristics are applied to rigorously identify the principal asymptotic class in the case of $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles $X_n=\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^{n}}(\mathcal{O}\oplus\mathcal{O}(n))$. We observe, in particular, that for $X_n$ of dimension at least four, the Conjecture $\mathcal{O}$ holds just for even values of $n$, and in these cases we falsify the original non-modified Gamma conjecture I.

papers.title: Secondary Chow Invariants beyond Lawson--Massey Products
papers.abstract: We construct secondary Chow invariants that cannot be recovered from Lawson--Massey realization. For every smooth complex projective curve $C$ of positive genus and every $n\ge2$, explicit cubical defining systems yield $n$ distinct Massey values in $\rm{CH}^{3}(C\times P^{2},1)$, with zero full indeterminacy, forming a cyclic group of order $n$. All corresponding triples have identical morphic classes and zero morphic, Lawson, and singular Massey brackets, despite nonzero target groups. The values are detected by the Weil pairing. We further construct secondary quotient classes of every finite order on smooth projective varieties with ample canonical bundle in every dimension at least two, and prove that generically finite pullbacks of coprime degree preserve their exact orders. These constructions obstruct integral and prime-local motivic formality, although the corresponding brackets become $\{0\}$ after reduction modulo every integer $m\ge2$. All specified values are torsion and vanish after rationalization.

papers.title: Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field
papers.abstract:
We study the rational canonical form of sparse random matrices over a finite field. Suppose $A_n\in\mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$ has independent and $\alpha_n$-balanced entries. We prove that if $n\alpha_n-\log n\to+\infty$, then, for every fixed collection of distinct monic irreducible polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the corresponding primary partitions of $A_n$ converge jointly to the same asymptotically independent Cohen-Lenstra distributions as in the uniform random matrix model. This strengthens the finite-field cokernel universality theorem of Lee (arXiv:2511.13070), which assumes $\alpha_n=c\log n/n$ for a fixed $c>1$, by resolving the additive endpoint case explicitly left open in his work. Moreover, our result extends universality from ordinary cokernels to the full rational canonical form. The condition is optimal for universality uniformly over fixed irreducible polynomials.
  Our proof uses the surjection moment method developed by Sawin and Wood (arXiv:2210.06279) over $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$, together with a refinement of Lee's Fourier estimates that retains the full leading-order decay. We also construct degree-$d$ critical sparse obstructions, suggesting a polynomial-dependent threshold of $1/d$ for irreducible polynomials of minimal degree $d$.

papers.title: Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations
papers.abstract: Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.

papers.title: Superconnections and Bott-Chern valued Riemann-Roch-Grothendieck for complex orbifolds, I
papers.abstract: We use flat antiholomorphic superconnections to study orbifold Chern character following the method introduced by Bismut, Shen, and Wei on general complex orbifolds. We show the uniqueness of orbifold Chern character by proving a Riemann-Roch-Grothendieck theorem for orbifold embeddings.

papers.title: Supercuspidal blocks and the local Langlands correspondence
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group defined over a non-archimedean local field $F$, and let $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ be a supercuspidal Bernstein block. In this paper, we define a cohomology class $[\mu_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ represented by a 2-cocycle that encodes the equivalence class of $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$. We then formulate a conjecture describing $[\mu_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ in terms of the enhanced $L$-parameter $(\varphi, \rho)$ attached to an irreducible representation in $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ via the conjectural local Langlands correspondence. Finally, we verify this conjecture for the local Langlands correspondence for non-singular supercuspidal representations constructed by Kaletha.

papers.title: Superlinear complexity of the $(3/2)^n$ steering word
papers.abstract: Write $(3/2)^n = m_n + \varepsilon_n$ with $m_n$ the nearest integer and $\varepsilon_n\in[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, and let $T=(t_n)$, $t_n=2m_{n+1}-3m_n$, be the resulting \emph{steering word}: the step-by-step record of the map $x\mapsto\tfrac32 x$ on the orbit of 1, coded by nearest-integer rounding. We prove that the subword complexity $p_T(k)$ of $T$ is superlinear, $p_T(k)/k\to\infty$. A pigeonhole argument reduces this to exponential pair repulsion of the orbit modulo one, which we establish by two applications of the $p$-adic Subspace Theorem: once in three variables, which handles all gaps between the two orbit points at once, and once in two variables (Ridout's theorem) for the single degenerate family of constant gap. The argument is completely formalized in Lean~4, together with the Subspace Theorem it uses.

papers.title: Supersingular Tate conjecture for irreducible symplectic varieties of known types: I
papers.abstract:
We prove that for a supersingular irreducible symplectic variety admitting suitable lifting to characteristic zero has Tate Chow motive if it is of deformation type $K3^{[n]}$, OG6 (with Artin invariant $
eq$ 4), or OG10 (with Artin invariant $
eq$ 12), and has supersingular abelian Chow motive if it is of $\mathrm{Kum}^n$-type (with Artin invariant $
eq$ 3). In particular, any product of those irreducible symplectic varieties satisfies the supersingular Tate conjecture for the whole $\ell$-adic or crystalline cohomology ring.

papers.title: Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veroneseans
papers.abstract: The Terracini locus of a projective variety tells us the sets of points at which Terracini's lemma will fail to recover the dimension of the corresponding secant variety. We study the Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veronese varieties, classifying several cases, including a complete classification of the Terracini loci of tangential varieties to rational normal curves. We also show that many Terracini loci involve only sets with "intratangent pairs" that lie on the same tangent space to the underlying Veronese variety. Finally, we give some applications to algebraic statistics, showing that osculating varieties of Veronese varieties are moment varieties for local mixtures of location families and connecting Terracini loci to local identifiability.

papers.title: Testing the non-vanishing of the Ceresa cycle of $X_0(N)$
papers.abstract: For a curve $C$ and a fixed degree-one divisor $e$ of $C$, we can embed $C$ into its Jacobian. This embedding induces an algebraic $1$-cycle on the Jacobian called the Ceresa cycle, which we denote by $\Cer(C,e)$. Although homologically trivial, Ceresa cycles of very general curves with genus $\geq 3$ are non-trivial under algebraic equivalence. It is generally unknown whether a very general curve admits a non-trivial Ceresa cycle modulo rational equivalence. In this paper, we explore the non-triviality under rational equivalence of the Ceresa cycle corresponding to the modular curve $X_0(N)$. By extending a method of Lupoian--Rawson involving computing the order of the shadow of the Atkin--Lehner involution $w_N$, we show $\Cer(X_0(kN),e)$ is non-trivial when $N = 57, 58, 77, 82, 85, 88, 91, 93, 111, 112, 115, 123, 133, 135, 141, 143, 145, 147, 155, 161$ for $k \geq 1$. Moreover, we detail an algorithm for computing the shadow of the Hecke operator $T_\ell$ for odd primes $\ell$ not dividing $N$, which can be used to determine the non-triviality of the Ceresa cycle of $X_0(N)$.

papers.title: The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry
papers.abstract: Amplituhedra are semi-algebraic sets of fundamental importance in particle physics. Their discovery initiated the field of Positive Geometry. We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.

papers.title: The Binder-DeMarco-Dupont Inequality
papers.abstract: In the setting of endomorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^k(\mathbb{C})$, a dimension formula for the measure of maximal entropy was conjectured by Binder and DeMarco in 2003, asserting that $$\mathrm{dim}_\mathrm{Hausdorff}(\mu)=\log d\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{\chi_i},$$ where $d$ is the degree of the (non-invertible) endomorphism and $\chi_i$'s are the Lyapunov exponents with multiplicity. Indeed, this is well-defined as all Lyapunov exponents are known to be positive due to Briend and Duval. The most significant progress is due to Dupont, who in complex-dimension 2, proved the dimension lower-bound holds; And recently by Genes, who proved the equality for two-dimensional polynomial skew-product maps which satisfy a Lyapunov exponent condition. Recently, He and Bianchi were able to find a family of simple counter-examples. In Appendix A we present a single ``hands on'' description of such a counter example, which is given by a quadratic polynomial skew-product. In this manuscript, we provide the proof, which was achieved by lightly prompting ChatGPT, of extending Dupont’s inequality to all complex dimensions. We wish to share this manuscript with the community as we believe that this provides a full picture of the recently settled Binder-DeMarco conjecture. We do not claim ownership of the proof.

papers.title: The Chow Ring of the 2-Sylow Subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}(4,2)$
papers.abstract: This paper provides a computation of the mod 2 Chow ring of the motivic \'etale classifying space of the finite group $\mathrm{Syl}_2(\mathrm{GL}(4,2))$. It outlines a general computation strategy, adapted from work by Burt Totaro, that has been largely automated by the author. This strategy can be used to compute more examples of Chow rings of motivic \'etale classifying spaces quickly.

papers.title: The Projective Reed-Muller Code from Quartic Curves in the Projective Plane
papers.abstract: We study the Hamming weight enumerator of the projective Reed-Muller code $\mathcal C_{2,4}$ over $\mathbf F_q$, with $\operatorname{char}(\mathbf F_q)>3$. We determine the geometrically reducible and singular contributions by combining incidence counts with counts of plane linear series on a fixed normalization. The line and conic configurations and the genus zero cases give explicit polynomials. The line-cubic and genus one cases give formulas involving class numbers. The genus two contribution is a finite sum over hyperelliptic models, using their point counts over $\mathbf F_q$ and $\mathbf F_{q^2}$ and their rational Weierstrass points. The remaining smooth contribution is the weighted point count distribution of nonhyperelliptic genus three curves.

papers.title: The Riemann Hypothesis on Young's Lattice
papers.abstract: This work establishes a novel structural connection between the Riemann Hypothesis and Young's Lattice through partition-indexed harmonic numbers and the Generalized Assembly Theorem. We establish a new family of equivalences for the conjecture, define the partition-based harmonic numbers $H_n^{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$, and reformulate the Riemann Hypothesis as the Young's Lattice equivalence: $$\sum_{\substack{k \in \mathbb{N} \\ \boldsymbol{\lambda} \, \vdash \, k}} \frac{H_n^{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}}{\boldsymbol{\lambda}!} \, a_k > \sum_{d \mid n} d$$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, where $\boldsymbol{\lambda} \vdash k$ denotes a partition of $k$, $\boldsymbol{\lambda}!$ is the partition factorial, and $a_k = \frac{1}{k} + \dots + \frac{1}{k^2}$ or $a_k=\log(k+1)$. We then prove the Generalized Assembly Theorem, which shows that the assembly sum $\mathfrak{S}_n^m = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \sum_{\boldsymbol{\lambda} \in \wp_k^{k+m-1}} H_n^{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$ equals $n$ for every excess parameter $m-1$, providing a systematic framework to analyze divisor bounds through the branch decomposition of the partition-indexed series. The resulting structure yields an exact, non-asymptotic realization of the divisors of $n$. Finally, we propose and explore a hierarchical expansion connecting the exponential of the Euler--Mascheroni constant, $e^\gamma$, to Multiple Zeta Values under Abel summability. $$e^\gamma = 1 + \sum_{a\ge2} \frac1{a!} \sum_{m\ge0} (-1)^m\zeta^{\mathrm{A}}(a+m) + \sum_{a,b\ge2} \frac1{a!\,b!} \sum_{m,n\ge0} (-1)^{m+n}\zeta^{\mathrm{A}}(a+m,b+n) + \cdots$$

papers.title: The span-squares adjunction
papers.abstract: We show a universal property of the span $\infty$-category that yields a description of functors defined on this category. For this, we view the span construction as a functor from double $\infty$-categories to $\infty$-categories, and show that this functor admits a right adjoint defined by the double $\infty$-categories of squares. As an application, we obtain a model for the localization of an $\infty$-category in terms of a span $\infty$-category and also give another proof of the model given by the relative nerve. Moreover, using the span-squares adjunction, we obtain new proofs of the equivalences between different models of algebraic $K$-theory, given by the $\Q$-, the $\oS$-, the cobordism model, and the squares construction.

papers.title: The theory of F-rational signature
papers.abstract:
F-signature is an important numeric invariant of singularities in positive characteristic that can be used to detect strong F-regularity. One would like to have a variant that rather detects F-rationality, and there are two theories that aim to fill this gap: F-rational signature of Hochster and Yao and dual F-signature of Sannai. Unfortunately, several important properties of the original F-signature are unknown for these invariants.
  We give a modification of the Hochster-Yao definition that agrees with Sannai's dual F-signature and push further the united theory to achieve a complete generalization of F-signature.

papers.title: The third unit in the adjoint tower of group involutions
papers.abstract: The functor $G\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(C_2,G)$ determines an adjoint tower through successive Eilenberg--Moore comparison functors. We prove that the unit of the third adjunction need not be an isomorphism, answering a question of Bergman. For the generalized dihedral group $H=(C_4\times C_4)\rtimes C_2$, with inversion action, we compute $F_3V_3H\cong H\times C_2$, with counit the first projection. The unit at $V_3H$ is injective, with underlying domain and codomain of cardinalities $20$ and $40$. For an arbitrary group $G$, let $E(G)=F_2V_2G$ and let $K_G$ be the kernel of the second counit. We prove that $K_G$ is central and that $F_3V_3G\cong E(G)/K_G[2]$, where $K_G[2]$ consists of the elements of $K_G$ whose square is one. The third unit at $V_3G$ is an isomorphism precisely when $K_G$ has no element of order four. A central extension of $H$ of order $128$ supplies such an element and yields the stated description of $F_3V_3H$.

papers.title: There are no Miyaoka--Kobayashi octics
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a reduced plane curve of degree $n$ with only ADE singularities. Using K\"ahler-Einstein metrics, Kobayashi proved an upper bound, in terms of $n$, for a sum of local invariants of the singular points of $C$. For even $n$ this bound had been obtained earlier by Hirzebruch and Ivinskis. Curves of even degree for which equality holds are called Miyaoka-Kobayashi curves, and the only known examples are three types of plane sextics. We show that there are no Miyaoka--Kobayashi curves of degree $8$, and additionally that a Miyaoka-Kobayashi curve of degree $10$ cannot be free. The key new ingredient is a new linear constraint on the singularities of such curves, obtained by differentiating Langer's orbifold Bogomolov-Miyaoka-Yau inequality.

papers.title: Total mutual visibility in Fibonacci and Lucas cubes
papers.abstract: A set of vertices is total mutual-visible if every pair of graph vertices has a shortest path whose internal vertices avoid the set. We prove that the total mutual-visibility numbers of the n-dimensional Fibonacci and Lucas cubes both have order ρⁿ/n, where ρ > 1 satisfies ρ³ = ρ² + 1. The eligible Fibonacci words are exactly those avoiding 11 for which zero padding avoids 0000. Their induced graph decomposes into fibres of recognizing subsets of maximal independent sets of a path, and each fibre is a Cartesian product of smaller Fibonacci cubes. Total visibility becomes open packing in these fibres. An elementary coloring and counting argument proves the order of growth. Typical degree and free-dimension estimates, together with a classical binary-code asymptotic, sharpen the normalized bounds to constants 4.032058… and 6.346255…. We give the cyclic analogue, an exact component inventory, and reproducible exact values through dimension 20 for Fibonacci cubes and 16 for Lucas cubes. Neither a leading asymptotic constant nor a closed formula in every dimension is established.

papers.title: Twisted group codes of dimension 2 and 3
papers.abstract: It is known that all group codes of dimension at most $3$ are permutation equivalent to abelian group codes. We prove that twisted group codes of dimension at most $3$ are monomially equivalent either to an abelian group code or to an irreducible constacyclic code, and in the second case we describe the code explicitly by means of a trace map. Monomial equivalence cannot be replaced by permutation equivalence, and the second case cannot be avoided: the ternary tetracode is an ideal of $\mathbb F_3[x]/(x^4+1)$ but it is not monomially equivalent to any group code. More generally, we give two infinite families, in dimensions $2$ and $3$, of irreducible constacyclic codes which attain the Griesmer bound, whereas every group code with the same length and dimension has smaller minimum distance.

papers.title: Two-Sided Dimension Bounds for the Peterson Hit Problem via Projections and Matrix Minors
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal P_k=\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_k]$ be the polynomial algebra over the prime field $\mathbb F_2$, viewed as an unstable module over the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra $\mathcal A$. The well-known Peterson hit problem asks for a minimal set of generators for the $\mathcal A$-module $\mathcal P_k$. This is equivalent to determining the dimension of the cohit space $(Q\mathcal P_k)_d=(\mathcal P_k/\mathcal A^{+}\mathcal P_k)_d$, where $\mathcal A^{+}$ denotes the augmentation ideal of $\mathcal A$, for every $k\geq1$ and positive degree $d$. Although solved in every degree for at most four variables, it remains a difficult open problem in general. Furthermore, given the limitations of current tools, explicitly determining the dimension of $(Q\mathcal P_k)_d$ in the general case appears out of reach. Motivated by these limitations, we establish explicit upper and lower bounds for this dimension for arbitrary positive integers $k$ and $d.$ Our method combines binary combinatorics, linear algebra, and graph and simplicial structures associated with the generating Steenrod squares. We characterize zero rows, count zero columns, and refine rank estimates using Adem relations. Minors and zero rows of the resulting smaller matrix yield further two-sided cohit bounds without determining a complete basis or computing the full hit rank.

papers.title: Type IIA String Theory and tmf with Level Structure
papers.abstract: We look at a new string$^h$ tangential structure first introduced by Devalapurkar and relate it to the $W_7=0$ condition of Diaconescu-Moore-Witten for type IIA string theory and M-theory. We show that a string$^h$ structure on the target space automatically satisfies the $W_7=0$ condition and we also explain when the $W_7=0$ condition gives rise to a string$^h$ structure. Devalapurkar initially constructed $MString^h$ in such a way that it orients $tmf_1(3)$; we extend Devalapurkar's result, showing that $MString^h$ orients $tmf_1(n)$. We compute the homotopy groups of $MString^h$ in the dimensions relevant for physical applications, and apply them to anomaly cancellation applications for certain compactifications of type IIA string theory.

papers.title: Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits\ for Positive Factorial Multiples
papers.abstract:
Let $\tau(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values. We show that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, some positive integer $m$ satisfies \[
  \tau(mk!)\leq
  \exp\!\left(O\!\left((\log k)^{2/3}(\log\log k)^{1/3}\right)\right). \] The proof combines unconditional results of Lenstra, Pila and Pomerance on smooth numbers in short intervals and on orders of genus-two Jacobians with a five-parameter family carrying a rational divisor class of infinite order. We encode rational divisor arithmetic, including the tests determining its branches, by a nonzero division-free integer circuit. A common finite sampling space yields circuits whose outputs collectively contain every prime at most $k$, and repeated squaring supplies the required factorial valuations. The circuit bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and GPT-6.1 Sol.

papers.title: Uniqueness of twisted linear periods
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let $\D$ be either $F$ or a quaternion division algebra over $F$. We prove that every irreducible smooth representation of $\GL_{p+q}(\D)$ has at most one linear period transforming under any prescribed character of $\GL_p(\D)\times\GL_q(\D)$.

papers.title: Unistationarity of Type II_l and Type V autocatalytic cores with nonnegative degradation
papers.abstract: We prove that reversible Type II_l autocatalytic cores with l at least three and Type V cores admit at most one positive stationary state when every degradation rate is nonnegative. The Type II result assumes source-minimality, while the Type V statement uses its literal normal form. Strictly positive reaction rate constants are retained throughout. A reduction to the fork skeleton, source-exhaustion identities and diagonal current criteria control both positive-loss and boundary cases, including internal chains. We also derive determinant estimates and local continuation results, with small-degradation existence and stability under the stated hypotheses. The main nonnegative-degradation uniqueness theorem is registered in Lean 4; the manuscript and supporting claim map distinguish the formal interface from additional conventional results.

papers.title: Unistationarity of Type II_l autocatalytic cores
papers.abstract: We prove unistationarity of reversible Type II_l autocatalytic cores with l at least three under strictly positive degradation. The source-minimal wiring forces source exhaustion and unit return tails, allowing comparison of positive stationary states through current ratios, chain reduction and a cyclic determinant argument. The proof includes separated stems and the exceptional coincident three-fork branch, with all internal chain species retained. Exact six- and seven-species reversible mass-action examples show that the minimality assumptions cannot be dropped: both admit two distinct positive stationary states with strictly positive rates and losses. The principal uniqueness theorem has a complete registered Lean formalization. The manuscript distinguishes that theorem, broader historical formal evidence and conventional exact calculations; the supplied claim map records the boundaries of each.

papers.title: Waring--Goldbach Problem: One square, four fifth powers and fifteen sixth powers
papers.abstract: We prove that for every sufficiently large even integer $n$, the equation $$ n = p_1^2 + p_2^5 + p_3^5 + p_4^5 + p_5^5 + p_6^6 + \cdots + p_{20}^6 $$ has a solution with all $p_j$ prime.

papers.title: Waring--Goldbach Problem: One square, four fifth powers and twenty-two seventh powers
papers.abstract: We prove that for every sufficiently large odd integer $n$, the equation $$ n = p_1^2 + p_2^5 + p_3^5 + p_4^5 + p_5^5 + p_6^7 + \cdots + p_{27}^7 $$ has a solution with all $p_j$ prime.

papers.title: Zero-divisor methods for absolute concentration robustness
papers.abstract: We study the relation between absolute concentration robustness and zero divisors in steady-state coordinate rings. Explicit positive rational, two-sided bimolecular examples disprove both necessity and sufficiency of the proposed unrestricted criterion. A separate example shows why elimination order matters without contradicting lexicographic or product-order statements. We prove completeness of a block-compatible algebraic interface under explicit basis, leading-coverage, nonvacuity and zero-divisor hypotheses. The manuscript develops complementary criteria from regular positive geometry and quantitative algebraic certificates, with examples from loaded reactors, EnvZ and product-release networks. Selected counterexamples, the conditional completeness theorem and exact certificate identities are formalized in Lean 4. Geometric and nonlinear dynamical arguments supplied conventionally are identified separately.
